Connect your Last.fm

Pull in your scrobbled albums so you can start journaling about them. Grab a free API key from your Last.fm account page — it takes about 30 seconds. Once connected, your username and key are remembered on this device indefinitely, so you won't need to reconnect next time you open the page — until you choose to forget them below.

Connect Spotify

Optional: use Spotify's catalog for artwork, tracklists, and genres instead of iTunes — often faster and more complete. Create a free app at the Spotify Developer Dashboard to get a Client ID and Client Secret (no redirect URI needed for this). Once connected, Spotify is used automatically for searches and new albums; iTunes is still the fallback if anything fails.

Add an album by hand

No Last.fm history for it, or want to log something manually? Search for it here — artwork and tracklist come from Spotify once connected above, or the iTunes catalog otherwise. Try "album by artist" (e.g. "Automatic for the People by R.E.M.") for the most precise match.

Add via streaming link

Got an Apple Music, Amazon Music, or Qobuz link for something the search above can't find? Paste it here. Apple Music links get pulled in with full artwork and tracklist automatically; other links are saved with a "listen on..." button on the entry.

Your Spotify stats

Log in with your Spotify account (different from the app connection above) to see your top artists, top tracks, recently played, and what's playing right now. This needs the page hosted at a stable URL — add that exact URL as a Redirect URI in your Spotify app settings first. It won't work opened as a local file straight from disk.

Live scrobbling

Bridges your Spotify listening straight to Last.fm: while this tab is open, it checks what you're playing every 20 seconds, updates "now playing" on Last.fm immediately, and submits a proper scrobble once a track has played long enough to count. Requires both your Spotify login above and Last.fm's API secret entered on the Connect page.
